subject: Local SI integration & data residency — pre-sprint coordination

From: Evelyn Schmidt <evelyn.schmidt@helix-consulting.de>

Cc: Kenji Sato <k.sato@kyoto-analytics.jp>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:22:00 +0200
Subject: Local SI partnership — DE data residency questions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Helix is running a discovery with two German enterprise prospects that will require local data residency (DE) and strong evidence around audit logs and key management. Before we scope workstreams for a local SI engagement, could you share your standard residency checklist and any constraints for the Private (VPC/on-prem) offering in DE? Also tagging Kenji from Kyoto — he will be the delivery lead for APAC/JP and wants to align on where requirements diverge.

High level asks:
- Where does Redwood require customer-managed KMS vs. Redwood-managed?
- Typical retention and audit-log retention supported by the Private control plane
- Any latency implications for local SIs when routing to your control plane in eu-central-1 vs. private deploy

If you have a short checklist or a template SOW that calls this out, that would help us scope the first sprint. Can we aim to sync next week?

Best,
Evelyn
Partner Lead — Helix Consulting
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Schmidt <evelyn.schmidt@helix-consulting.de>
Cc: Kenji Sato <k.sato@kyoto-analytics.jp>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:05:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Local SI partnership — DE data residency questions

Evelyn — thanks, this is exactly the kind of ask we expected. Looping in Vanessa (partnerships / SI enablement) and Sergio (solutions engineering) so we can put together a concise checklist and an initial integration matrix.

Short answers inline:
- KMS: we support both. For Private deployments we recommend customer-managed KMS (HSM/KMS) for regulated customers; hosted Dedicated can be Redwood-managed if contractually approved.
- Audit logs: Private control plane ships audit logs with configurable retention; default 90 days, can be extended for enterprise plans. We can provide snapshots and immutable exports for SOC evidence.
- Latency: local SI install (on-prem or VPC) is designed to avoid cross-region token roundtrips; if you use Redwood Private with a local control plane in DE, latency is minimal. If routing to hosted control plane in eu-central-1 we recommend co-locating inference capacity or using a dedicated pool.

Vanessa / Sergio — can you assemble the lightweight checklist + example SOW and the integration matrix Kenji referenced? Evelyn / Kenji — are you available for a 30m sync on Wednesday 13 May 09:00-11:00 CEST or Thursday 14 May 14:00-16:00 CEST?

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Partnerships Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Schmidt <evelyn.schmidt@helix-consulting.de>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Kenji Sato <k.sato@kyoto-analytics.jp>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 08:43:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Local SI partnership — DE data residency questions

Hi all — I attached a first-pass checklist and an integration matrix (partner-integration-matrix.xlsx) that maps roles, evidence, and owner for each compliance item. I also exported the residency requirements doc for Germany (residency_requirements_DE_v1.pdf). Highlights:

- KMS: customer-managed recommended for private; if customer prefers Redwood-managed we require a contract clause and a minimum Dedicated commitment for isolated tenancy.
- Audit logs: support for immutable exports; default retention 90 days but we have packages for 1/3/7 year retention tied to enterprise SLAs.
- Networking: SI will need VPN/Direct Connect to the Private control plane; we have a template network diagram and a list of firewall ports.

For the sprint I propose:
1) Day 0: alignment call (30m) to confirm scope and data residency must-haves
2) Day 1–2: SI tech ramp + security questionnaire completion (Helix lead)
3) Day 3–4: Private control-plane deploy in a staging VPC and smoke tests
4) Day 5: handover and runbook delivery + evidence package for procurement/legal

Evelyn / Kenji — if that sequence looks reasonable, confirm preferred sync slot and I will send calendar invites and a shared Drive folder (link below).

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partner Operations — Redwood Inference

Attachments: partner-integration-matrix.xlsx, residency_requirements_DE_v1.pdf
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Thanks Vanessa — matrix looks good. A couple of implementation notes from eng:
- For Private installs that must keep inference keys on-prem, we recommend enabling KV-prefix caching with strict local-only policy to avoid cross-region syncs. That will require a small config change in the runtime (I can push a patch to the infra repo we use for partner deploys).
- We should prepare an abbreviated runbook for on-call SRE handoff; Helix will want an escalation matrix for the first 30 days after go-live.

Evelyn/Kenji — I can host the staging deploy on our eu-central-1 partner pool and work with your infra lead to schedule the deploy window. Proposal: 18 May for staging deploy, 20 May for customer smoke tests. If that timeline is tight for you, tell us and we will move things around.
